items.title: SemReuse: auditing reused filter results
items.summary: SemReuse proposes storing semantic-filter outputs as materialized views and using inferred predicate relationships to provisionally accept or skip tuples. A pooled stratified audit checks the resulting answer and triggers additional evaluations when needed.
items.implication: Its contribution is a certification procedure around fallible reuse decisions. The abstract reports up to 15.4× fewer evaluations in its experiments; this does not establish savings for every workload.

items.title: SemViews: prior labels guide fresh certification
items.summary: SemViews uses prior query labels, embeddings and helper scores to order tuples, then certifies the answer with fresh stratified oracle samples. The preprint reports 28–45% fewer oracle calls across four workloads.
items.implication: Both SemViews and SemReuse study certified reuse, but their use of prior state and auditing procedures differ. Their reported savings should not be read as a head-to-head comparison.

items.title: NousDB: token costs enter query planning
items.summary: NousDB’s October 21 revision describes a DataFusion-based engine with semantic algebra, token histograms and batching under context-window constraints. The first version appeared October 20.
items.implication: Token volume and batching fidelity become planning concerns alongside relational rewrites. The profile retains the paper’s claims as author-reported results.

items.title: JEVDB: decision models and join pruning
items.summary: JEVDB uses typed decision models for filters, joins, classification and ranking, with selective escalation to generative models. Its join execution combines relational reduction with semantic candidate screening.
items.implication: This explores a different execution choice from generating text for every decision. The reported evaluations use SemBench and the join-oriented Shelob workload.

items.title: Repeatability is an evaluation dimension
items.summary: Same Query, Different Answer studies repeated executions of semantic workloads at temperature zero. It distinguishes changes to individual operator decisions, complete answers and aggregate quality.
items.implication: A stable average score need not mean a stable answer. Repeated execution and item-level reporting are relevant when comparing engines or validating a cached result.

items.title: CADENZA: exposing tasks inside an operator
items.summary: The PACMMOD publication develops intent-specific task DAGs and task-extended relational algebra for semantic operators. It is associated with SIGMOD 2027; the preprint was already available in June 2026.
items.implication: The newly added profile covers a previously cataloged source. Planning includes task decomposition and routing, rather than treating each semantic call as a single fixed implementation.

sources.label: Publisher citation record and online publication date

items.title: Snowflake caches identical calls within a query
items.summary: Snowflake documents automatic, best-effort response caching for identical AI_COMPLETE text calls within a single query. Cache hits are not billed.
items.implication: This is exact-call reuse within one execution. It does not provide the cross-query, predicate-level certification studied by the reuse papers.

items.title: Databricks updates extraction and chart parsing
items.summary: Databricks’ October 2 release notes describe a new standard-mode ai_extract checkpoint, with a vendor-reported 2.3× speed improvement and higher quality at unchanged cost. ai_parse_document also returns chart data as structured JSON.
items.implication: These are changes to extraction functions. The announcement does not establish an end-to-end semantic-query optimization result.

items.title: IMLane: separating inference and database scheduling
items.summary: IMLane uses process-level AI-function execution and separates inference scheduling from the database scheduler. Its publication and abstract describe integrations with OceanBase and DuckDB.
items.implication: New to this catalog, but earlier than this issue’s reporting window. It concerns execution of AI functions, including predictive models, rather than a new semantic-operator language.

items.title: Featurized-Decomposition Join: pruning through features
items.summary: FDJ extracts features and combines inexpensive comparisons to prune semantic-join candidates, with statistical quality guarantees described in the preprint.
items.implication: This newly profiled paper was already in the bibliography. Its verified preprint date is December 2025, so it is background reading rather than a new October result.

items.title: Snowflake adds evaluation and configuration search
items.summary: Two public previews support measuring AI-function quality, cost and consistency, and searching prompt/model configurations against a common dataset and metric. A selected configuration can become a reusable SQL AI function.
items.implication: These September 21 announcements precede the reporting window. They supply context for function-level optimization; they do not establish joint optimization of an entire relational plan.

items.title: BigQuery Graph reaches general availability
items.summary: Google’s September 1 announcement describes native GQL graph traversal alongside SQL, with access to BigQuery ML and AI functions in the same query.
items.implication: This is older, adjacent infrastructure for combining graph, relational and model-based computation. It is not evidence of a new semantic-operator optimization technique.

issues.title: Certified reuse, execution choices, and repeatability
issues.summary: Research on semantic-filter reuse, task-level planning and query execution, alongside product updates to caching and extraction.
issues.introduction: This issue covers selected developments from September 25 through October 24, 2026. The research raises three distinct questions: which previous decisions can be reused, which computation should implement an operator, and how reliably repeated runs reproduce an answer. Product releases address narrower parts of these questions through exact-call caching and extraction improvements.
